top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rests on three separable, load-bearing contributions: the tractable pricing friction, staggered contracts with an estimable policy rule, and the welfare-based synthesis. The work is mature, has been revised and extended rather than abandoned after 2008, the zero lower bound and the 2021-23 inflation, and has shaped both research and policy practice. No earlier prize recognised this pricing-friction and rule core. The main cost is attribution, since Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler are excluded by the three-name cap, so the citation should credit the foundations and make no claim over the estimated-DSGE tradition. P002 (Kiyotaki, Moore) has cleaner attribution and a distinct mechanism, but a narrower footprint and original identification that came mostly from later work. It is a sound second choice, and I rank it above no award.
